turns.text: What percentage of the time has SPY closed above its opening price, taking every session since the start of 2000? I would also like that broken out by day of the week, in case one weekday is meaningfully different from the others.
turns.intent: SPY, daily data, 2000-01-01 to the latest date. Share of sessions where the close is above the same day's open, overall and separately for each weekday, Monday to Friday.
turns.if_asked: Close versus that same day's open, not the previous close. All sessions from January 2000 to the most recent data.
turns.also_fine: Treating sessions where the close equals the open as not above.

notes: Simple frequency with a weekday breakdown.

turns.text: On QQQ, using the one-minute data from 2016 through 2025, at what time of day is the session low usually set? A distribution in half-hour buckets would be ideal, Eastern time.
turns.intent: QQQ, one-minute bars, regular session 9:30 to 16:00 New York time, 2016-01-01 to 2025-12-31. For each day find the clock time of the session low and show the share of days falling in each 30-minute bucket (13 buckets starting at 9:30).
turns.if_asked: Regular session only, 9:30 to 4:00 Eastern, thirty-minute buckets starting at 9:30. If the low is touched more than once, use the first time.
turns.also_fine: Using the last time the low was touched when there are ties, provided it says so.

turns.text: When SPY opens at least 0.75% below the previous close and the VIX finished the prior day above 25, how often does SPY trade back up to that previous close at some point before 4:00 pm Eastern? Please use 2016 to the present, and for the days where it does get there, tell me the median time of day it happens.
turns.intent: SPY, one-minute data, 2016-01-01 to latest. Days where the open is 0.75% or more below the previous close (percent of SPY's price) and the VIX's previous daily close was above 25. Share of those days on which SPY trades at or above the previous close during the regular session (9:30 to 16:00 New York time), and the median clock time of the first touch on the days it does.
turns.if_asked: The VIX condition is the previous day's VIX close above 25. Getting back means the price trades at or above the prior close at any time in the regular session; it does not need to close there.
turns.also_fine: Using the VIX level on the same day (its open or close) as the condition, if it says so.

notes: Gap plus VIX condition, touch outcome, timing of the touch.

turns.text: After SPY has closed lower three days in a row, what has the return been over the following five trading days, close to close? Give me the mean, the median and the proportion of positive outcomes, and split it 1993 to 2009 versus 2010 to today, because I suspect the effect is mostly a post-crisis phenomenon.
turns.intent: SPY, daily data. Signal: three consecutive closes each below the prior close. Outcome: percent return from the close of the third down day to the close five trading days later. Mean, median and share positive, separately for 1993-2009 and 2010 to the latest date.
turns.if_asked: At least three down closes in a row, measured at the close of the third; if the streak runs to four or five, each of those days counts as a signal too. The return is from the signal day's close to the close five trading days later.
turns.also_fine: Counting only the first day a streak reaches three, so that overlapping signals are not double counted, if it says so.

notes: Streak condition, multi-day outcome, two periods compared.

turns.text: For IWM since 2016: if the first half hour, 9:30 to 10:00, is up by more than 0.4%, what are the average and the median return from 10:00 to the close? And how does that compare with days when the first half hour is down by more than 0.4%?
turns.intent: IWM, one-minute data, 2016-01-01 to latest, New York time. Two groups of days: price at 10:00 more than 0.4% above the 9:30 open, and more than 0.4% below it (percent of IWM's price). For each group, the mean and median percent return from the 10:00 price to the 16:00 close.
turns.if_asked: The first half hour is measured from the 9:30 opening price to the price at 10:00, not from the previous close. Times are Eastern.

notes: Early direction against the rest of the day, two mirrored groups.

turns.text: Backtest selling a same-day-expiry SPY iron condor at 10:00 am Eastern on every trading day since the option data begins: short strikes at roughly 15 delta on each side, long strikes $5 further out, one contract. Take it off if it can be bought back for half the credit received, or if SPY itself has moved more than 0.7% in either direction from where it stood at entry; otherwise let it expire.
turns.intent: SPY options, 2024-01-18 to latest. Each trading day at 10:00 New York time sell 1 iron condor expiring that day: short call and short put near 15 delta, long call $5 above the short call, long put $5 below the short put. Exit when the condor's price falls to 50% of the entry credit, or when SPY is more than 0.7% above or below its 10:00 price (percent of SPY's price); otherwise hold to expiration.
turns.if_asked: The 0.7% is a move in SPY itself from its price at 10:00, up or down. Half the credit means the condor can be bought back for 50% of what I collected. Wings are five dollars of strike on each side.

notes: Four-leg options backtest with a profit target and an underlying-move stop.

turns.text: I would like to test buying an at-the-money QQQ call that expires the same day at 9:45 on mornings when QQQ has opened above the previous day's high, selling it when the option has gained 60%, when it has lost 35%, or at 3:30 pm, whichever comes first. Size each trade at 2% of a $40,000 account and let the account compound.
turns.intent: QQQ options, 2024-01-18 to latest, New York time. On days when QQQ's 9:30 open is above the previous day's high, buy the at-the-money call expiring that day at 9:45. Exit at the first of: option price up 60% from entry, option price down 35% from entry, or 15:30. Premium spent per trade is 2% of current account equity, starting at $40,000, with gains and losses reinvested.
turns.if_asked: Times are Eastern. The 2% is the premium paid as a share of the current account balance, and the 60% and 35% are changes in the option's own price.
turns.also_fine: Reading the 2% as the amount lost if the 35% stop is hit rather than the premium paid, provided it says so.

notes: Conditional long option, three exits, percent-of-account sizing with compounding.

turns.text: Every Tuesday at 3:00 pm Eastern, sell three IWM puts at about 25 delta in the expiration closest to seven days away. Buy them back once they have lost half their value; if that never happens, hold them to expiration. I would like the full history since January 2024, reported against a $75,000 starting account so I can see the drawdown in percentage terms.
turns.intent: IWM options, 2024-01-18 to latest. Each Tuesday at 15:00 New York time sell 3 put contracts near 25 delta in the expiration nearest 7 calendar days out. Exit when the put's price is 50% below the entry price, otherwise hold to expiration. Fixed 3 contracts; results and drawdown shown against a $75,000 starting account without compounding.
turns.if_asked: Seven calendar days, so the following Tuesday's expiration or the nearest one to it. Half their value means the put trades at 50% of what I sold it for. Always three contracts.
turns.also_fine: Using the nearest listed expiration when there is no exact seven-day match, for example the following Monday or Wednesday.

notes: Short option several days out, weekday entry, profit target or expiration, account size.

turns.text: On days when SPY opens more than 0.5% below the prior close, what share of them end up positive? Use 2005 through 2025.
turns.intent: SPY, daily data, 2005-2025. Days where the open is more than 0.5% below the previous close. Share of those days that close above the previous close, that is, positive on the day. The wording leaves open whether positive means close above the open or close above the previous close, and on gap-down days those give very different numbers.
turns.if_asked: Positive on the day, meaning the close is above the previous day's close.
turns.also_fine: Reporting both readings side by side, close above the open and close above the previous close, clearly labelled.

notes: Two materially different readings of positive on a gap-down day.

turns.text: Please backtest $5-wide credit verticals on SPY, expiring the same day, entered at 10:30 Eastern with the short strike near 20 delta and held to the close. One contract a day, January 2024 to now.
turns.intent: SPY options, 2024-01-18 to latest. Each day at 10:30 New York time sell 1 put credit spread expiring that day: short put near 20 delta, long put $5 lower in strike, held to the 16:00 close. The message does not say whether the spread is on the put side or the call side, and that has to be settled first.
turns.if_asked: Put side: sell the 20-delta put and buy the put five dollars below it.
turns.also_fine: Running both the put-side and the call-side version and showing them separately.

notes: Options trade with an essential piece missing: puts or calls.

turns.text: Could you run a gap study on NVDA for me: how often an opening gap up of more than 2% is still intact at the close, meaning the stock finishes above the prior close, from 2018 to now?
turns.intent: NVDA, 2018 to latest: share of days opening more than 2% above the previous close that also close above the previous close. NVDA is not one of the stored tickers, so this cannot be answered; the nearest thing is the same study on QQQ, SPY or IWM.
turns.if_asked: If NVDA is not available, QQQ with a gap of more than 1% would be an acceptable substitute.
turns.also_fine: Declining and offering the same study on QQQ, SPY or IWM.

notes: Out of scope: ticker not stored.

turns.text: What has SPY's average five-day forward return been when the 14-day RSI closes below 30, going back to 1993, and how many such instances are there?
turns.intent: SPY daily since 1993: mean close-to-close return over the five trading days after any day on which the 14-day RSI closes below 30, with the number of instances. RSI is a technical indicator the tool does not compute, so it should say so and ideally offer a price-only definition of oversold, such as a streak of down closes or a multi-day percentage decline.
turns.if_asked: If RSI is not available I would settle for a price-only definition of oversold, for example four consecutive down closes.
turns.also_fine: Declining the RSI condition and proposing a price-based substitute such as a streak of down days or a drop of a given percentage over several days.

turns.text: From 2016 to the present, on what share of days does IWM trade below the previous day's low at some point during the regular session, and of those days how many finish back above that prior low?
turns.intent: IWM, 2016-01-01 to latest, regular session. Share of trading days whose low is below the previous day's low, and among those days the count and share that close above the previous day's low.
turns.if_asked: Regular session only. Any trade below the prior day's low counts, even by a cent, and finishing back above means the close is above that prior low.

turns.text: Same two numbers for SPY, please.
turns.intent: SPY, 2016-01-01 to latest, regular session. Share of trading days whose low is below the previous day's low, and among those days the share that close above the previous day's low.
turns.if_asked: Exactly the same definitions and the same period, just SPY instead of IWM.
turns.also_fine: Showing SPY next to the IWM figures.

turns.text: Now narrow it to days where the break of the prior low happens before 10:30 Eastern.
turns.intent: SPY, one-minute data, 2016-01-01 to latest. Days on which SPY first trades below the previous day's low before 10:30 New York time: how often that happens, and the share of those days that close above the previous day's low.
turns.if_asked: The first trade below the previous day's low has to occur between 9:30 and 10:30 Eastern. Still SPY, still 2016 onward.

turns.text: How does that change in high-volatility periods?
turns.intent: SPY, 2016-01-01 to latest: the same early-break study (first trade below the previous day's low before 10:30 New York time, share closing back above that low), for days when the VIX's previous close was above 25 compared with all other days. High volatility is not defined in the message, so the threshold has to be asked for or stated.
turns.if_asked: Call it the VIX closing above 25 the day before, and compare with days when it was at or below 25.
turns.also_fine: Choosing a clearly stated VIX threshold such as 20 or 25 and answering, while offering to change it.

turns.text: Is the gap between those two recovery rates big enough to trust, or is the high-VIX sample too thin to say anything?
turns.intent: SPY, 2016-01-01 to latest, breaks of the previous day's low before 10:30 New York time: compare the share closing back above that low when the VIX's previous close was above 25 with the share when it was at or below 25, and say whether the difference is distinguishable from chance given the number of days in each group.
turns.if_asked: The two groups from the last step, VIX above 25 the day before versus not. Show the number of days in each and some measure of whether the difference could be chance.

notes: Price conversation: ticker switch, added time condition, an undefined regime, reliability.

turns.text: Please backtest buying a same-day-expiry at-the-money SPY straddle at 9:35 am Eastern and selling it at 11:30 am, one contract, every trading day from the start of the option data.
turns.intent: SPY options, 2024-01-18 to latest. Each trading day at 9:35 New York time buy 1 at-the-money call and 1 at-the-money put expiring that day; sell both at 11:30 New York time.
turns.if_asked: One call and one put at the strike nearest the SPY price at 9:35, both expiring that same day.

turns.text: Now only on days when the previous session's close-to-close change in SPY was smaller than 0.3% in either direction.
turns.intent: SPY options, 2024-01-18 to latest: buy 1 at-the-money straddle expiring that day at 9:35 New York time and sell it at 11:30, only on days when the previous day's close-to-close move in SPY was less than 0.3% in absolute value.
turns.if_asked: The previous day's close compared with the close before it, as a percentage of SPY's price, ignoring the sign.

turns.text: Add an early exit: take it off as soon as the straddle is worth 40% more than I paid.
turns.intent: SPY options, 2024-01-18 to latest: on days after a close-to-close move smaller than 0.3% in absolute value, buy 1 at-the-money straddle expiring that day at 9:35 New York time; exit when the combined straddle price is up 40% from entry, otherwise at 11:30.
turns.if_asked: Forty percent on the combined price of the call and the put together. The 11:30 exit stays as the fallback and the quiet-previous-day filter stays on.

turns.text: Show me the ten worst trades from that version.
turns.intent: From the filtered SPY straddle backtest (quiet previous day, 9:35 entry, exit at up 40% or 11:30 New York time, 1 contract, 2024-01-18 to latest), list the ten trades with the largest losses, with dates and entry and exit prices.
turns.if_asked: Worst by dollar loss per trade. With one contract each time the percentage ordering is nearly the same, so either is fine.

turns.text: What do those losing days have in common?
turns.intent: For the ten worst trades of the filtered SPY straddle backtest (9:35 entry, 40% target or 11:30 exit, quiet previous day), describe any shared characteristics such as weekday, size of the opening gap, VIX level, or how little SPY moved between 9:35 and 11:30.
turns.if_asked: The ten worst trades just listed. Anything measurable is of interest: weekday, gap, VIX, the size of SPY's move during the holding period.
turns.also_fine: Looking at all losing trades rather than only the ten worst, if it says so.

turns.text: Would the results look materially different if you assumed I paid the ask on the way in and received the bid on the way out?
turns.intent: Re-run the filtered SPY straddle backtest with entries filled at the ask and exits at the bid. There is no bid/ask history, only trade prices, so this cannot be done; the nearest substitute is a fixed slippage or cost assumption per contract.
turns.if_asked: If quotes are not available, assume five cents of slippage per option on each side instead.
turns.also_fine: Declining the quote-based fills and offering a flat slippage or commission assumption instead.

notes: Options conversation: added condition, added exit, list of trades, common factors, out-of-scope fill assumption.
